result:
Workspace is clean of build artifacts, with the source fixes in place. Here's the full report:

## What changed (before → after)

| Issue | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Root metadata | `app/layout.tsx` served **"InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes"** for every page — a leftover from before the pivot to Lumina | Fixed to Lumina's real title/description/OG/Twitter card |
| Blog crawlability | `app/blog/page.tsx` was `'use client'`, fetched `/api/posts` (404) client-side — crawlers without JS saw only "Loading posts…" | Rewritten as a server component reading from `lib/posts.ts`; added `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` (SSG, `generateStaticParams`) so all 12 posts render full content + per-post metadata with zero JS required |
| Sitemap | `app/sitemap.ts` had a `TODO` and only listed 4 static URLs — all 12 blog posts were invisible to it | Now emits 16 URLs (4 static + 12 posts) |
| AEO | No FAQPage/Article/Organization structured data anywhere; `/faq` 301-redirected to `/#faq`, which didn't exist on the homepage (dead link) | Added a real FAQ section with 5 Q&As (facts pulled from the existing `/pricing` and `/features` copy, nothing invented) + `Organization`, `SoftwareApplication`, and `FAQPage` JSON-LD on the homepage, `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post |
| GEO/LLMO | No `llms.txt`; the only real content (blog) wasn't readable without JS | Added `public/llms.txt`; blog is now plain static HTML |
| Legacy content | 12 blog posts, 100% about the old product (InboxZap email cleanup) — zero mention of Lumina, serving under Lumina branding with no disclosure | Kept live (preserves existing rankings/backlinks) but each now carries an honest one-line notice: *"published when this product was InboxZap... we've since become Lumina"* with a link to `/features`. Did **not** rewrite the posts to fake relevance, and did **not** 301 them into Lumina pages — both would show searchers something false. |

## Crawler's-eye verification (curl evidence)

Ran a real `npm install && npm run build` (succeeded, all 12 posts prerendered as SSG) and `next start` locally to confirm, no-JS:
- Home: `<title>Lumina — The AI Meeting Assistant for Teams</title>`, 3 JSON-LD blocks (Organization/SoftwareApplication/FAQPage)
- `/blog`: lists all 12 real post titles in plain HTML (previously: empty spinner)
- `/blog/post-1`: full article body + legacy notice + `BlogPosting` JSON-LD, no JS needed
- `/sitemap.xml`: 16 `<loc>` entries (was 4)
- `/llms.txt`: 200
- `/faq` → 308 → `/#faq` → 200 with real FAQ content (was a dead redirect)

## What I didn't do, and why

- Didn't rewrite the 12 legacy posts to pretend they're about meeting assistants, and didn't 301-redirect them into Lumina pages — both are bait-and-switch for anyone clicking through from search.
- Didn't buy/trade backlinks or touch anything off-domain.
- Didn't build a Lumina-specific content backlog from real keyword data — the GSC export is 100% pre-pivot (InboxZap queries), so there's no query data for the current product yet. Logged this gap and a starting hypothesis list in `content/backlog.md`.

## Next measurement (schedule this)
- Re-pull GSC in **~4-6 weeks** (around 2026-12-22 to 2027-01-05) once Lumina URLs/the newly-sitemapped posts have had time to be recrawled and indexed.
- Track: (1) whether `/blog/*` posts pick up impressions for their existing topics now that they're crawlable, (2) whether the homepage FAQ content starts appearing in AI Overviews/answer engines for Lumina queries, (3) CTR on legacy posts after the rebrand notice (watch for any bounce-rate change on those pages specifically).
